blocks.text: ILIGAN CITY – Fourteen Higaonon tribal families who were alleged victims of New People’s Army (NPA) atrocities in Impasugong, Bukidnon are undergoing a three-day trauma healing process. Lt. Colonel Jeorge R. Jallorina, commanding officer of the Army’s 8th Infantry Battalion (8IB), said the Nov. 24 to 26 healing process opened with a “panastas,” a traditional Higaonon ritual led by Datu Lord Sarinao, Impasugong municipal tribal chieftain. The ritual, which gathered the families and members of the community, was meant to honor their experiences and draw strength from their culture and tradition.
